E1.evidence: Issue #46 (chadrockey, 2013-11-07) gives a two-command reproducer and the observed effect: 'To duplicate issue: rosrun tf2_ros static_transform_publisher  1 2 3 0 0 0 1 parent child / rosrun tf2_tools view_frames.py / It doesn't show the parent and child in this case, just shows no frames received.' (https://github.com/ros/geometry2/issues/46). The maintainer tfoote fixed it in a2f8eea ('adding support for static transforms in python listener. Fixes #46').

E2.evidence: Step 1: the units are two ROS nodes that interact only through a ROS topic: the static_transform_publisher executable of tf2_ros (tf2_ros/src/static_transform_broadcaster_program.cpp, whose StaticTransformBroadcaster does 'publisher_ = node_.advertise<tf2_msgs::TFMessage>("/tf_static", 100, true);') and the view_frames.py node of tf2_tools, which runs the in-process tf2_ros python TransformListener ('listener = tf2_ros.TransformListener(buffer)'); the python listener thread only does 'rospy.Subscriber("/tf", TFMessage, self.callback)'. Step 2: the failure is a topic-name mismatch crossing the boundary: the provider publishes the transform on /tf_static and the consumer subscribes only to /tf, so the transform never reaches the consumer; a consumer that subscribes to /tf_static (the C++ tf2_ros::TransformListener at the same revision does: 'message_subscriber_tf_static_ = node_.subscribe<tf2_msgs::TFMessage>("/tf_static", 100, ...)') receives it. Step 3: not deployment wiring: the minimal resolving change adds a subscription to /tf_static and a static-aware buffer entry point (tf2_py set_transform_static) to the consumer side, i.e. the consumer's referenced interface changed; a remap of /tf_static onto /tf would deliver the message but insert it as a non-static transform that expires from the buffer, so it is not the resolution taken. Steps 4-5: not build or firmware. Step 6: eligible, interface kind topic.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the provider's published TFMessage on /tf_static is meant to feed the consumer's listener; the failure was observed with both nodes running and the data never arriving. No other operation is supported by the source.

E4.evidence: Observed failure (no data): 'It doesn't show the parent and child in this case, just shows no frames received.' (https://github.com/ros/geometry2/issues/46); view_frames.py emits 'digraph G { "No tf data received" }' when the buffer is empty.

units.name: tf2_ros
units.revision_basis: The reporter names no version. 17e5713 is the hydro-devel commit the fix was applied to (parent of a2f8eea; the ROBUST record's bugzoo bug-commit). It is one commit after tag 0.4.9 (2013-11-06, the day before the report); tf2_ros/src/static_transform_broadcaster.cpp, static_transform_broadcaster_program.cpp, tf2_ros/src/tf2_ros/transform_listener.py, tf2_tools/scripts/view_frames.py and tf2_py/src/tf2_py.cpp are identical between 0.4.9 and 17e5713 (the diff touches only tf2/include/tf2/LinearMath/Vector3.h and tf2/src/buffer_core.cpp). The static_transform_publisher node is not changed by the resolution, so resolved_rev equals broken_rev.

units.name: tf2_tools
units.revision_basis: view_frames.py (tf2_tools 0.4.9) runs the tf2_ros python TransformListener and the tf2_py binding in its own process; all three packages live in this repository at the same revision. Broken: 17e5713 (see provider). Resolved: a2f8eea (2013-12-26, 'adding support for static transforms in python listener. Fixes #46'), which edits tf2_ros/src/tf2_ros/transform_listener.py and tf2_py/src/tf2_py.cpp used by the node; released in 0.4.10 (2013-12-26). view_frames.py itself is unchanged.

loudness_evidence: No diagnostic at build, connection, or activation: the publisher advertises /tf_static and the listener subscribes to /tf, both succeed, and the consumer simply reports an empty graph at run time: 'It doesn't show the parent and child in this case, just shows no frames received.' (https://github.com/ros/geometry2/issues/46).

resolution.summary: Commit a2f8eea: the tf2_ros python TransformListenerThread additionally subscribes 'rospy.Subscriber("/tf_static", TFMessage, self.static_callback)' and forwards each transform with 'self.buffer.set_transform_static(transform, who)'; tf2_py gains the binding 'set_transform_static' (setTransformStatic), which calls 'bc->setTransform(transform, authority, true);' so the static transform is stored as static in the BufferCore.
resolution.evidence: Diff of a2f8eea: '+        rospy.Subscriber("/tf_static", TFMessage, self.static_callback)' ... '+    def static_callback(self, data):' / '+        who = data._connection_header.get('callerid', "default_authority")' / '+        for transform in data.transforms:' / '+            self.buffer.set_transform_static(transform, who)' and '+  {"set_transform_static", setTransformStatic, METH_VARARGS},' with '+  // only difference to above is is_static == True' / '+  bc->setTransform(transform, authority, true);' (https://github.com/ros/geometry2/commit/a2f8eea04f95c9abb0e4d7557d796e84fb13a32a). The issue was closed by the commit ('Fixes #46'); no run of the reproducer against the fixed listener is shown in the source.

notes: Failed-condition class: the provider publishes on a topic (/tf_static, latched) that the consumer's listener did not subscribe to, while the consumer listened on /tf, which this provider never publishes; no named class covers a consumer lacking a subscription to the provider's topic, so 'other' is used (element_removed_or_renamed would only fit if the provider had moved the data from /tf to /tf_static relative to what the consumer was written against, which the source does not document). The inventory lists topic:/tf with only the consumer side because the static_transform_publisher does not publish it; it is included because the consumer's subscription to it is the element the failed condition contrasts with. The C++ tf2_ros::TransformListener already subscribed to both /tf and /tf_static at 17e5713, so C++ consumers of the same publisher were unaffected (a different composition). The ROBUST record classifies the case as 'Incomplete implementation of an API (no CWE)' in package tf2_py and notes the fix 'was released as part of version 0.4.10'. The reporter's hydro release is not stated; the report is dated one day after tags 0.4.8 and 0.4.9, and the relevant files are unchanged between 0.4.9 and the fix parent.
